Something you actually do learn in marketing 101 is that marketing actually isn't about directly selling products. The goal of it is to leave a positive impression of the product in the consumer's mind. Think about Coke ads. The reason they spend billions on advertising even though they have a global stranglehold on the soft drink market is not to try to get you to buy more Coke, but to maintain a positive image of the drink in your mind. What's the first image you associate with Coke? Maybe it's one of the thousands of ads that show a nice cool refreshing coke being poured on ice and those wispy almost iconic bubbles of carbonation gently bopping off the ice right before some attractive and healthy individual guzzles it down with a smile and satisfaction. The positive image (and nice taste) completely outweighs the health consequences of drinking Coke so most of us don't even really think twice before picking one up. The nonstop ads keep that positive image rolling.

Another interesting factoid - ads also don't focus on price. Consumer behavior is irrational. If there are two products that are near identical but one costs more then they tend to associate the higher price with a better quality or more desirable product even if there's no reason whatsoever to do so.
